_comment: Every entry is a control this project claims to have, and the exact edit that
should break it. `node scripts/mutate.mjs --all` applies each one to the real
source, runs the real suite, and demands that the named test goes red.
AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md §6: a green suite is evidence that nothing currently
disagrees with a control, not that the control exists. This file is where that
distinction is made mechanical -- and where 'nobody audits the auditor' (§7) is
answered, because each mutation is stated precisely enough to be re-run by
ADD AN ENTRY WHEN YOU ADD A CONTROL. Not later, and not only when a control
looks fragile: the two worst defects of 2026-09-03 were both in code written
that same hour specifically to enforce verification honesty, and both looked
finished. `find` must match EXACTLY ONCE or the run reports INCONCLUSIVE.
The `expect` field is a substring of the test name that must appear among the
failures. Without it, ANY red suite would count as the control working -- which
is how a mutation that broke something unrelated gets recorded as proof.

mutations.guards: the apron extends further than the sea plane, so the modelled rectangle's edge is not visible through the water as a tray
mutations.expect: the ground reaches further than the water

mutations.guards: the apron's coarse grid lands exactly on the fine mesh's edges, so the two abut instead of gapping or overlapping
mutations.note: This mutation could not bite at all until APRON_STEP_MULTIPLE moved into WORLD. The test used to compute the step itself, so no change to the renderer could fail it. Writing this entry is what found that.
mutations.expect: the apron grid lands exactly on the modelled rectangle's edges

mutations.guards: each cloud deck owns its material, so the low one can fade while the high one is still overhead
a deck you have climbed above stops drawing, instead of rendering its far rim as a white crescent
mutations.expect: at the orbit Mark was flying

mutations.guards: both pages bloom the same world the same way, because the renderer uses the shared BLOOM object rather than a copy of its values
mutations.note: Mutating to an equal-valued literal, not a different one: the point is that a COPY is the defect, even when the numbers happen to match today. That is precisely how the two pages drifted apart in the first place.
mutations.expect: the tuned render values are what they are meant to be

mutations.guards: props.js resolves every manifest id by its own name, so prop-models.js does not need a second table that must agree with it
